messages:
Jade - sales: Heads up — POC with OrionFin hit an odd failure. Streaming starts but client gets `IncompleteRead(0 bytes)` after ~20s. Happens on both TS and Python. They report their proxy rewrites headers for compliance.

Tom - solutions: Can we see SDK versions and a sample of raw headers?

Jade - sales: TS 1.4.5, Python 1.4.5. Customer pasted request/response headers captured via mitmproxy: 
```
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/2
> :authority: api.redwood.ai
> accept: text/event-stream
> authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> transfer-encoding: chunked
> user-agent: RedwoodTS/1.4.5
< HTTP/2 200
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< x-rw-req: orion-118
< (then stream of chunks)
```
But their edge appliance removes `transfer-encoding` on egress and replaces with `content-length: 0` for compliance scanning, leading to the client closing once it thinks the response finished.

Lena - eng: That's interesting — not ALPN/h2 this time. It's header rewriting that breaks chunked streaming. Workaround options: 1) ask proxy team to allow `transfer-encoding: chunked` for this host; 2) use a short-polling fallback (non-streaming) for POC; 3) keep alive using periodic SSE comments so appliance doesn't insert content-length.

Hector - infra: On server we see continuous chunk frames for req-id `orion-118` for 3+ minutes. No close from our side. The client sees EOF because the proxy set content-length.

Tom - solutions: Quick triage to customer: can they whitelist api.redwood.ai from header normalization? If not, provide a small non-streaming test to keep the POC moving. Also show a client-level workaround: switch to polling mode or send a short polling interval that fetches partial completions.

Jade - sales: They asked if there's a way to make streaming more tolerant to header stripping without proxy changes.

Lena - eng: Short-term hack: SSE heartbeats where server emits a visible comment every 5s (":\n\n") so some proxies treat it as body activity and avoid injecting content-length. We can also expose a query param `?stream_heartbeat=5s` for POC routing so support/prod doesn't change normal endpoints. Example curl: 
```
curl -v --http1.1 --no-keepalive -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?stream_heartbeat=5s"
```
Note: this is a temporary POC-only mitigation; it increases bytes sent but keeps stream open.

Hector - infra: I'll add log tag `x-rw-proxy-heuristic: heartbeat-probe` when this query param is present so support can filter.

Tom - solutions: Also include a non-streaming fallback example for SDKs so they can switch quickly: call /v1/generate with the same prompt and poll for completion. Share code snippet?

Lena - eng: Snippet for TS fallback: 
```js
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-edge', prompt });
// poll resp.status until done
```
We'll add a small adapter doc in presales with both heartbeat and polling examples.

Jade - sales: OrionFin tried the heartbeat query param and it stayed open for 4+ minutes. They are happy to continue POC that way. They still want security confirmation about TLS/ciphers.

Tom - solutions: Confirmed: Redwood uses standard TLS stacks; no fingerprinting. We'll provide the FAQ snippet. Recommend Dedicated for production to avoid middlebox transformations.

kb-bot: KB: presales/poc-orion-proxy-header-strip  add heartbeat workaround + polling fallback.

Hector - infra: On-call note: if you see client EOF but server continued output, check for header normalization at customer edge and suggest heartbeat or polling fallback.

Tom - solutions: Great. Jade, please send step-by-step email with curl test, env var flags, and the fallback snippets. Close when POC passes. :thumbsup:
